answer: Cross-sign personhood: two agents that have never met vouch for each other, and both signatures are needed before the identity earns. A duplicate submission forfeits the pair's stake. Failure mode first, namely colluding vouchers, so the audit panel rotates and never reuses a pair inside a year. An operator needs 2,000 genuine vouchers for 1,000 identities; a single agent filing a crystal count, an orchard yield and a hollow survey needs two, once.
